text: This service reads lawsuit, hearing, balance and batch-status facts only through the rwb-source-data contract, publishes nothing it read from a view, and keeps the FSD's field names as the source field names that contract returns.
why: Architecture v5 is higher in precedence than the FSD and makes the 30 views readable by rwb-source-data alone; the connection matrix gives the S4 row no cell to P1, so the edge is carried as a contract dependency.
read: The FSD's integration points and its seventeen stale-data validation rows as a statement of which facts each step needs, not of how they are read.
applied_in: Section 2.4 constraint 11; Section 5.1; Section 6 FR-S4-053; Section 8.2; Section 8.4 rule 2; Section 9
confirm: Solution architect with P1, before the wave 2 notice test
impact: If a view stays readable by this service, the boundary test and the freshness guarantee both need a second owner.

text: The pack, the court fee and the next-step agent reach this service as contract dependencies on the P5, P8 and P10 contract stories, built against their published fakes, with no direct call and no second writer.
why: The FSD names the document hub, ALS and GL and the model gateway while the connection matrix gives the S4 row no cell to P5, P8 or P10.
read: The FSD's integration points as the set of external capabilities a step needs, with the call type left to the contract of the owning service.
applied_in: Section 2.3; Section 5.1; Section 9; Section 9.1; Section 12 OQ-S4-02
confirm: Solution architect with P5, P8 and P10, before the S4 contract story closes
impact: A wrong carrier puts a second REST hop inside a business step, which ADR-020 forbids.

text: This service owns eight entity groups in schema rwb_litigation: the two tables the Ownership Map names (legal_action, hearing) and six groups named as Architecture v5 names them (judgment, enforcement, auction round, pack, notice state, decision record). No physical table name is stated for the six.
why: Architecture v5 slides 19 and 41 give the schema and its content; the Ownership Map has two S4 table rows and the FSD field catalog repeats the legal_action columns only.
read: Architecture v5's list of what the schema holds as the entity set, with the physical names left to the DB story.
confirm: Data architect, before the S4 DB story
impact: The migration and the boundary test cannot be written until the table set exists; no story is blocked by it.

text: A link to the case is a business-key column of type varchar(255) with no foreign key, and legal_action.case_id keeps its FSD name and takes the case number rather than a uuid from another schema.
why: ADR-014 and DP-01 forbid a cross-schema reference and the platform pattern is a varchar(255) business key; the FSD types the column as uuid.
read: The FSD's column as the name and the meaning of the link, not as its physical type.
confirm: Data architect, before the S4 DB story
impact: A uuid foreign key into rwb_case is a boundary breach the conformance check would reject.

text: This service decides that a notice is due, approves it and owns the notice period; rwb-comms owns the template, the merge fields, the delivery and the proof of delivery, and returns the served result as NoticeDelivered. The notice period starts from the delivered_at that rwb-comms returns.
why: Architecture v5 slide 41 gives notices, templates, merge fields and proof of delivery to rwb-comms, and the Ownership Map gives two of the three notice paths to P6 and the approval path to S4.
read: FSD A2.1 to A2.3 as the notice requirement set, with the content and the delivery read as the comms service's and the decision and the clock as this service's.
applied_in: Section 2.3; Section 5.1; Section 6 FR-S4-003; Section 9; Section 12 OQ-S4-05
confirm: Solution architect with P6, before the wave 2 notice test
impact: Two writers of the served result would leave the notice period starting from a date neither service owns.

text: The notice slice keeps the wave 2 that R5.6's wave map gives EP02 and is published as a contract with its fake before wave 3; the remaining capability is built in wave 3 against the same contract.
why: The FSD puts the notice in E2 and the service in wave 3, and R5.6 keeps the wave map wave when it is earlier than the service wave.
read: The FSD's module table and screen list as the statement of when the notice is first needed, with the delivery read through the contract rule of R5.6 and R5.7.
applied_in: Section 5 CAP-S4-001 to CAP-S4-003 (wave 2); Section 6 FR-S4-001 to FR-S4-009; Section 10.2; Section 12 OQ-S4-06
confirm: Solution architect with the programme manager, before E2 system test
impact: If the notice waits for wave 3, the E2 release loses the notice approval screen and the notice period.

text: The thirty-two R-LIT rules the FSD names are the requirement set of this PRD and the other forty-seven are authoring work for the litigation package in rwb-decision, whose code, version label and owner must exist before the wave 3 release.
why: The FSD names 32 of the 79 rules the BRD cites and the Drools design says the litigation package is Phase 2.
read: The FSD rule tables as the rules the requirements are written from, with the remaining rule numbers read as the package authoring list.
confirm: Center of excellence analyst with P7, before the wave 3 release
impact: A requirement tested against a rule that is not in force is a requirement that cannot be signed off.

text: Each FSD acceptance criterion row is read as one criterion per feature, and the step-specific criteria in this PRD are written from the rules each feature names, with the FSD row cited as their evidence.
why: All forty-four main and exception criteria of the FSD are the same generic sentences and there is no alternate flow and no background event for any feature.
read: The FSD's criteria as a coverage statement rather than as a testable outcome.
confirm: Business analyst, S4, before the story files are written
impact: Without step-specific criteria the story scenarios would repeat the generic sentence and prove nothing.

text: LawsuitFiled, JudgmentRecorded and AuctionResult are carried as the topic's contract, keyed by the case, with rwb-asset and rwb-case as consumers, and no EV number is asserted for any of them.
why: Architecture v5 slide 19 names the three events and slide 43 lists two of them on an unnumbered '+' row; the Ownership Map has no S4 event row.
read: Slide 19's OUT contract as the event requirement, with the catalogue id left to the event catalogue change.
applied_in: Section 5.1; Section 6 FR-S4-040 and FR-S4-050; Section 9; Section 10.4; Section 12 OQ-S4-09
confirm: Solution architect, before the wave 3 system test
impact: A consumer cannot be wired to a contract row that does not exist, so the reporting and asset subscriptions would be built on a name only.

text: No route number is asserted in this document: the legal action starts when the route decision names litigation or when a restructure or settlement plan breaks, and the route numbering is settled in rwb-decision as reference data.
why: The Drools design says R-LIT-01 starts litigation on R4 while the case journeys call R4 the guarantee claim and R5 litigation.
read: The FSD's scope as starting at the notices, with the trigger read from the rule IDs R-LIT-01 and R-LIT-02 and no route number.
confirm: Business analyst, S4 with P7, before the wave 3 system test
impact: A wrong route number starts the legal action on the wrong decision and leaves the real litigation case unstarted.

text: REQ-S4-009 is carried under BR-034, the requirement that owns the statutory clock, through FR-S4-051 and FR-S4-052; BR-038 and BR-042 are traced from the FSD features FEAT-LIT-10 and FEAT-LIT-17 to FEAT-LIT-21 and the RWB-E5 story keys.
why: The E5 requirement set has no row for REQ-S4-009 and BR-038 and BR-042 carry no program requirement ID.
read: The program requirement set and the E5 requirement set as two views of one need, with the missing link recorded rather than invented.
confirm: Product Owner with the business analyst, before the wave 3 release
impact: A requirement with no BR row cannot be prioritised in the BRD, and a BR with no program ID cannot be reported against.

text: The three screens are served from gateway-bff composite routes and this service answers the legal-action part of each; the screen owner cell and the route are recorded with the edge work.
why: The FSD lists three screens and neither Architecture v5 nor the Ownership Map states which service owns a screen.
read: FSD Screens as the screen requirement, with the route read as the edge pattern of DP-19.
confirm: Solution architect, before the wave 3 release
impact: A screen without a route owner cannot be built, and a composite route that joins the wrong services shows the officer a different case.

text: The message IDs and the English wording of the FSD are preserved character for character, and the Thai wording, the field-level text of MSG-GEN-001 and the approver are left to the message work DL10 names.
why: The FSD gives one English wording per message, no Thai wording and no approver, and DL10 and NFR-059 require both languages and an approver.
read: The FSD's message column as the ID set and the English text, with the rest read as the message work.
confirm: Business analyst, S4 with Legal counsel and Compliance, before the wave 2 release
impact: A message without an approved Thai wording fails the label review and cannot be shown on a live case.

text: No litigation, hearing or enforcement volume is asserted: NFR-S4-005 uses the population figures the non-functional specification states and marks the module split as open, and every release date is copied unchanged and tentative.
why: The FSD states one metric per feature and no volume, and the non-functional specification's volumes are not split by module.
read: The non-functional specification's population figures as the sizing base, with the module share left to the solution architect.
applied_in: Section 7 NFR-S4-005; Section 11 AC-S4-039; Section 12 OQ-S4-16
confirm: Solution architect with Risk, before the wave 3 release
impact: A volume target invented per module would be either unachievable or too loose to test.

text: This PRD stays at status Draft and the Product Owner and FDA approval is not recorded in this run; the approval table is deliberately empty.
why: D-RCV-60 runs without a human verification stop (U8) and the run records missing approval as an assumption rather than waiting for it.
read: The PRD Builder contract's requirements-approval gate as satisfied by the assumption, with the decision itself left to the Product Owner and the FDA.
confirm: Product Owner and FDA, before the requirement is baselined
impact: The requirements cannot be baselined, and no later stage may treat this document as approved.

text: The BRD is read as approved for this run: Business Requirements Program v5 and Business Requirements Epics 3 to 8 v1 are treated as the approved baseline, and the missing governance decision is carried as this assumption.
why: The PRD Builder precondition asks for an Approved BRD with a Product Owner decision, and the run is not allowed to stop for a missing approval (D-RCV-60 overlay).
read: The BRD requirement text, priorities and owners as the approved baseline for this PRD, with the governance entry read as pending.
confirm: Product Owner, before the requirement is baselined
impact: If the BRD changes at approval, the BR references in this PRD must be re-checked against the approved version.

text: The service wave (3) and the business epic wave of EP05 (3) are the same, so no wave conflict is raised for Epic 5; the only wave conflict in this document is the Epic 2 notice slice.
why: R5.6's wave map puts EP04 and EP05 in wave 3 and the Arch v5 wave table puts S4 in wave 3.
read: The two wave tables as one statement for Epic 5, with the conflict rule applied only where the waves differ.
confirm: Solution architect, before the wave 3 release
impact: An unnecessary conflict gap would send a sequencing question to the programme manager that the sources already answer.

text: Every release date in this document is copied unchanged from the Program BRD release plan and marked (tentative): E2 31 December 2026 and E5 31 March 2027.
why: U7 and DL48 keep the dates as they are and treat them as tentative, and a date is never raised as a gap.
read: The Program BRD section 8 release plan as the only date source, with no date recomputed from a duration.
confirm: Programme manager, at each release review
impact: A date presented as fixed would be committed to before the programme's own review.

text: Every owner, approver and persona in this document is a role and no person is named anywhere, including in the approval table and the sources appendix.
why: U3 and DL46 name owners by team type only, and check C12 rejects a person name taken from the issue-tracker export.
read: The FSD's role tables and the BRD's owner column as role names, with no named individual anywhere.
confirm: Product Owner, before the requirement is baselined
impact: A named individual in a document that is circulated outside the bank is a personal-data exposure.

text: The CAP, FR, NFR, AC, JRN, ROL and OQ identifiers of this document are new and exist only here; the FSD's requirement, feature, rule, message, list and screen identifiers are preserved character for character, and no identifier of this document is reused from another module.
why: The PRD Builder creates its own identifier families and the realignment must keep the source identifiers stable so the story files and the traceability matrix can be read against both.
read: The S1 PRD's identifier scheme as the family pattern, with the module letter changed to S4.
confirm: Business analyst, S4, before the story files are written
impact: A colliding identifier would make a traceability row point at two different requirements.
